Working while in college not only helps students finance their education, it also assists in developing essential job and life long learning skills, and provides opportunities to network and conne…
competitors.text:
# Student Employment

## WELCOME

Student employment is an integral part of the educational and professional development of UA students. Working while in college not only helps students finance their education, it also assists in developing essential job and life-long learning skills, and provides opportunities to network and connect with faculty, staff, and fellow students who can help with the transition to life at UA. The experience gained is instrumental in preparing students for the job market after graduation and beyond.

## Post a Job

## Apply Now

## SEOTY Award

## Upcoming: 2026 On-Campus Student Job Fair

Human Resources and the SGA will partner together in hosting the 2026 On-Campus Student Job Fair. In 2025, we had over 400 students in attendance, participation from 20 departments, and 3 student raffle prize winners.

If you are an on-campus department interested in participating this fair, get added to our contact list by emailing uastudentjobs@ua.edu.

Contact us

## HERE ARE SOME USEFUL LINKS

The Department of Human Resources advertises undergraduate and graduate student assistant positions, both on-campus and off-campus. These student positions are compensated on an hourly basis, with payments made via direct deposit for the student’s personal use. For opportunities related to educational expenses, we recommend contacting the Financial Aid office to explore Work Study options or contacting the Graduate School for Graduate Assistantships. For further details, please refer to the links below.

---

findings.title: No single passage answers “live job finder for students” (best covers 25% of its terms)
findings.evidence: Best passage (52% into the page): “Set your preferences and we’ll scout live careers pages, read the details, and bring back matches worth your time.” — covers live; missing job, finder, students.
findings.impact: AI search answers are built from passages that match the question. When no passage covers the query, the engine quotes a competitor instead.
findings.fix: Add a one-paragraph direct answer under the H1 that uses the terms “job”, “finder”, “students” naturally, e.g. “FirstRole is [one factual sentence that answers “live job finder for students” using those words]”
findings.verify: Re-run; the answer passage card should show ≥80% coverage within the first 20% of the page.

findings.title: Not in the top 10 for “live job finder for students”
findings.evidence: 10 results sampled (US/English); neither https://firstrole-tinyfish-ai.vercel.app/ nor its redirect target appeared. It also did not appear for its own site: query, so indexing itself is in doubt. Ranking formats: 6 product / landing, 3 other, 1 blog / guide.
findings.impact: AI search tools (ChatGPT search, Perplexity, AI Overviews) pick sources from the same top results; a page outside them is effectively invisible for this question.
findings.fix: Make the page answer the query directly (see the Answer-ability finding). The words “finder”, “students” never appear on the page — use them in the title, H1 or opening paragraph where accurate. Study the top competing result (ziprecruiter.com, 0 words, 0 headings) in the Search tab and cover what it covers. Confirm the page is indexed in Search Console and listed in the sitemap.
findings.verify: Re-run the same query after publishing; the Search tab shows the position directly.

findings.title: Only 64 words reached the extractor
findings.evidence: Fetch returned 64 words from https://firstrole-tinyfish-ai.vercel.app/; the raw HTML body contains ≈183 words of text.
findings.impact: There is almost nothing for a retrieval system to quote. AI answers will cite a page that says more.
findings.fix: Add a direct, factual paragraph under the H1 that states what this page is and answers the target query; keep key facts in visible text, not images or tabs.
findings.verify: Re-run; extracted words should exceed 300 for a content page.

findings.title: No Open Graph tags
findings.impact: Open Graph drives the preview card when the page is shared in chat apps, social feeds and some AI answer UIs; missing tags mean a bare link.
findings.fix:
<meta property="og:title" content="FirstRole — Find your way in">
<meta property="og:description" content="Set your preferences and we’ll scout live careers pages, read the details, and bring back matches worth your time.">
<meta property="og:image" content="https://firstrole-tinyfish-ai.vercel.app/og-image.png">  (1200×630 px)
findings.verify: Re-run SignalScope: the Technical tab reads the live <head> via TinyFish Fetch (raw HTML) and will show the new value.

findings.title: No JSON-LD structured data
findings.evidence: No <script type="application/ld+json"> block in the HTML.
findings.impact: Structured data tells search engines and AI systems what the page *is* (an article, a product, an FAQ) and unlocks rich results. Without it, type has to be inferred from prose.
findings.fix:
Add a JSON-LD block to <head>, for example:
<script type="application/ld+json">
{"@context":"https://schema.org","@type":"WebPage","name":"FirstRole — Find your way in","url":"https://firstrole-tinyfish-ai.vercel.app/","description":"Live job and internship discovery with evidence-backed matching, clear visa details, and a shortlist that stays fresh."}
</script>
Use Article, Product, FAQPage or SoftwareApplication when they fit the content.
findings.verify: Validate at https://validator.schema.org, then re-run SignalScope.

findings.title: No sitemap.xml
findings.evidence: https://firstrole-tinyfish-ai.vercel.app/sitemap.xml was not found and robots.txt lists no Sitemap.
findings.impact: Without a sitemap, discovery of this page depends entirely on internal links; new or deep pages are indexed later or not at all.
findings.fix: Generate a sitemap listing https://firstrole-tinyfish-ai.vercel.app/ (Next.js: app/sitemap.ts; WordPress: Yoast/RankMath) and reference it from robots.txt with Sitemap: https://firstrole-tinyfish-ai.vercel.app/sitemap.xml
findings.verify: Re-run SignalScope: the sitemap row should show the page as listed.

findings.title: Title is 28 characters (shorter than typical)
findings.impact: A short title gives search engines little to match the query against and often gets rewritten.
findings.fix: Extend the title with the page's main topic, e.g. <title>FirstRole — Find your way in – Find your way in .</title>
findings.verify: Re-run SignalScope: the Technical tab reads the live <head> via TinyFish Fetch (raw HTML) and will show the new value.

findings.title: No canonical link
findings.impact: Query-string, trailing-slash and tracking variants of this URL can be indexed as duplicates and split ranking signals.
findings.verify: Re-run SignalScope: the Technical tab reads the live <head> via TinyFish Fetch (raw HTML) and will show the new value.

findings.title: No Twitter/X card tag
findings.impact: X and some link-unfurling tools fall back to a plain link instead of a rich card.
findings.verify: Re-run SignalScope: the Technical tab reads the live <head> via TinyFish Fetch (raw HTML) and will show the new value.

findings.title: No robots.txt
findings.impact: Everything is crawlable (good for visibility) but you have no place to declare your sitemap or AI-crawler preferences.

findings.title: No llms.txt
findings.impact: Optional, but a growing number of AI tools read /llms.txt to find the site's canonical, most-important pages in plain Markdown. It is a cheap way to steer which URLs assistants read first.
findings.fix:
Publish https://firstrole-tinyfish-ai.vercel.app/llms.txt:
# firstrole-tinyfish-ai.vercel.app
> One-line description of the site.

## Key pages
- [Page title](https://firstrole-tinyfish-ai.vercel.app/): what this page answers
findings.verify: Re-run SignalScope; the llms.txt row turns Present.

summary: firstrole-tinyfish-ai.vercel.app scores 34/100 (F) for “live job finder for students” — fundamental blockers prevent this page from being found or read. Strongest area: metadata & structure (11.5/20); weakest: search visibility (0/30). Fix first: No single passage answers “live job finder for students” (best covers 25% of its terms); Not in the top 10 for “live job finder for students”; Only 64 words reached the extractor.
limitations: Search positions come from one TinyFish Search sample (US, English) at audit time; they are directional, not a universal rank. robots.txt rules are evaluated for the exact path only; HTTP headers (X-Robots-Tag), Search Console data and backlinks are not inspected. Browser observations are agent-reported.
